articles.title: One found dead inside burned-out vehicle in Bharatpur
articles.summary: Police in Bharatpur discovered a dead body inside a vehicle that had caught fire on the service lane of the East‑West Highway. The vehicle was traveling along the highway when it ignited, and investigators are looking into the cause of the fire.

articles.title: For people with disabilities, surviving Nepal’s floods was only the beginning
articles.summary: The article examines how Nepal’s recent floods have left people with disabilities facing ongoing challenges beyond the immediate disaster. While many survivors struggled to find safe evacuation routes, those with mobility impairments encountered additional hurdles such as inaccessible shelters, lack of wheelchair assistance, and limited medical support. Humanitarian groups and government agencies are working to address these gaps, but systemic barriers—like inadequate infrastructure, insufficient disability‑friendly planning, and delayed aid distribution—persist. The piece highlights personal stories of resilience, calls for inclusive disaster response policies, and urges stronger coordination between NGOs, local authorities, and disability advocates to ensure that future emergencies do not repeat these shortcomings.

articles.title: Rybakina beats Gauff to book US Open final against Sabalenka
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina rallied after dropping the first set to defeat Coco Gauff, securing her place in the US Open women's singles final. She will meet defending champion Aryna Sabalenka for the title, marking Rybakina's first appearance in a US Open final.

articles.title: Landslide dams Solukhumbu river, spurring downstream flood warnings
articles.summary: A recent landslide has blocked the Solukhumbu River in Nepal, creating a temporary dam on the Hunga Khola. Water is spilling over the makeshift barrier, prompting authorities to issue flood warnings for downstream communities. Officials warn residents to stay clear of the riverbanks as the risk of a sudden breach remains high, urging preparedness and evacuation measures where necessary.

articles.title: PM Shah, New Zealand counterpart Luxon discuss flood response
articles.summary: Prime Minister Balendra Shah of Nepal expressed gratitude to New Zealand for a NZ$2 million humanitarian aid package following recent floods. In talks with his New Zealand counterpart, Christopher Luxon, Shah also appealed for New Zealand’s backing in securing climate‑related loss and damage financing to help Nepal cope with future climate‑induced disasters.

articles.title: Kushe Aunshi honours fathers, keeps ancestral traditions alive
articles.summary: Kushe Aunshi, also known as Gokarna Aunsi, was observed across Nepal as devotees offered prayers and gifts to their fathers and performed rituals to honor departed ancestors. Temples and homes saw families gathering to light lamps, present sweets, and recite traditional hymns, reinforcing the cultural importance of filial respect and ancestral remembrance. The festival, rooted in Hindu tradition, continues to sustain age‑old customs and strengthens community bonds throughout the country.

articles.title: Kim Jong Un wants North Koreans to have more (state-sanctioned) fun
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is pushing a new policy to boost consumer spending and provide state‑sanctioned leisure for citizens. The government is promoting luxury malls and personal pampering, channeling wealth through state‑controlled avenues while restricting informal markets. This move aims to placate a growing middle class and shift the country’s image from deprivation to modest prosperity, but it also tightens the regime’s control over economic activity.

articles.title: Nepal prepares Krishnabhir bypass as temporary fix remains uncertain
articles.summary: The Nepalese government is constructing a 12‑km bypass road on the opposite bank of the Trishuli River to replace the landslide‑prone Krishnabhir section of the Prithvi Highway, which remains closed. Officials say the temporary repair work is uncertain, prompting the accelerated upgrade to ensure connectivity between Kathmandu and the northern districts. The project, overseen by the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, aims to restore trade and travel routes vital for local economies, while residents and transport operators await a definitive timeline for the highway’s full reopening.

articles.title: Yemen’s Houthis reach strategic island at mouth of vital shipping lane
articles.summary: Yemen's Houthis have seized a strategic island at the mouth of a crucial Red Sea shipping lane, raising concerns over disruptions to global oil shipments and threatening Saudi Arabia's economy, which heavily relies on the route after the Hormuz Strait was effectively closed due to the Iran conflict.

articles.title: Five bridges on Bheri Corridor remain unfinished after six years
articles.summary: Six years after construction began, five bridges on the Bheri Corridor in western Nepal remain unfinished, stalled at foundations and half-built pillars. The project, intended to improve road access to the remote Dolpa district, was originally contracted for completion within three years. Delays have left the infrastructure incomplete, hindering connectivity and economic development for local communities. Officials from the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport have faced criticism over contract management and funding issues, while residents continue to rely on limited and unsafe routes.

articles.title: Nepal estimates Rs2.34 billion to rebuild flood-hit education sector
articles.summary: The Nepalese government has allocated Rs2.34 billion to restore the education sector after the August 26 Bhotekoshi floods. The disaster damaged 18 schools in Rasuwa District, halting classes for more than 9,000 students. The funding aims to rebuild classrooms, replace equipment, and resume normal schooling for the affected children.

articles.title: Water starts flowing through landslide-dammed Hunga Khola, easing flood risk
articles.summary: A landslide in Solukhumbu district blocked the Hunga Khola river, creating an approximate 100‑metre-long natural dam and raising concerns of downstream flooding. Local authorities warned residents of possible flood threats. By Friday, water began to flow through the dam, reducing water levels and easing the immediate flood risk for communities downstream.

articles.title: Modi, Putin hold talks in New Delhi on trade, defence
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in New Delhi to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation. Topics on the agenda included civil nuclear energy, fertiliser production, defence collaboration, critical minerals, manufacturing, railways and steel. An Indian source said the talks aim to deepen trade and strategic ties between the two countries.

articles.title: Government begins receiving chemical fertiliser from India ahead of wheat season
articles.summary: The Nepalese government has started receiving two consignments of diammonium phosphate (DAP) and one consignment of urea fertilizer from India via Birgunj, under a bilateral government-to-government agreement. A total of 60,000 tonnes of chemical fertilizer are being imported to support the upcoming wheat planting season, aiming to boost agricultural productivity.

articles.title: Arghakhanchi man gave up a job in South Korea to build a farm in his village
articles.summary: Khem Pandey, originally from Arghakhanchi, left a well‑paid job abroad after 13 years in India, Malaysia and South Korea to return to his native village in Nepal. He has invested over Rs 100 million to develop a large‑scale farm that produces milk, vegetables and staple crops, aiming to boost local agriculture and create jobs. His story highlights the growing trend of diaspora entrepreneurs channeling overseas earnings into rural development.

articles.title: Man dies after electric car catches fire in Bharatpur
articles.summary: A 56-year-old man died on Friday after his electric car veered off the East‑West Highway in Bharatpur, Nepal, and caught fire. The driver was trapped inside the vehicle when the fire broke out, leading to his death.

articles.title: Prime Minister Shah to highlight Nepal’s outsized climate burden at UN
articles.summary: Nepal's Prime Minister Shah will highlight the country's climate burden at the UN and press for financial support to recover from the Bhotekoshi floods.

articles.title: Philippine ferry fire death toll jumps to 35
articles.summary: A ferry operating in the Philippines caught fire, engulfing the vessel that was carrying over 130 passengers. Thick smoke and extreme heat initially prevented rescuers from entering the ship. As the rescue effort progressed, the death toll rose to 35 people. The incident highlights the challenges faced by emergency teams in maritime disasters and raises concerns about safety standards on passenger ferries in the region.

articles.title: Decade-old alternative to a vital Prithvi Highway link remains on paper
articles.summary: The Krishnabhir stretch of the Prithvi Highway, known for its susceptibility to collapse, highlights a critical gap in Nepal's transport network: the absence of a parallel route across the Trishuli River. Although a backup road was proposed nearly ten years ago, the plan remains unimplemented and exists only on paper. The article discusses the risks posed by the deteriorating highway section, the longstanding but stalled alternative route project, and the broader implications for connectivity and safety in the region.

articles.title: Saptari childbirth on street outside hospital raises questions over Nepal’s free maternity care
articles.summary: A woman in Saptari was forced to give birth on a pavement outside a government hospital after her husband could not pay the required Rs3,200 for medical tests. The incident highlights a stark gap between Nepal’s policy of free maternity care and the reality of accessing emergency healthcare services, especially for low‑income families. It raises concerns about the affordability of ancillary costs, the capacity of public hospitals, and the need for policy reforms to ensure truly universal maternal health coverage.

articles.title: UTL licence lapses, company seeks more time to clear Rs31 billion dues
articles.summary: The telecommunications firm UTL missed the September 4 deadline to renew its operating licence after failing to pay the required renewal fee and outstanding dues totaling Rs31 billion. The Nepalese government has warned that the licence cannot be reinstated until all arrears are cleared, and UTL has appealed for an extension to settle the amount.

articles.title: What’s on in Kathmandu Valley this week
articles.summary: The article provides a weekly roundup of cultural and community events happening across Kathmandu Valley. It highlights art exhibitions, live music performances, workshops, and various community gatherings. Several events are organized as fundraisers to support flood‑affected communities, detailing venues, dates, and participating groups. The piece encourages residents to attend, enjoy local creativity, and contribute to relief efforts.

articles.title: Book Review: An ice factory, the great famine and the mystery of missing Dalit workers
articles.summary: The Kathmandu Post reviews "White Elephant," a book that intertwines the story of an ice factory, the historic Great Famine, and the disappearance of Dalit laborers. The reviewer highlights how the narrative forces readers to confront both external oppressors and the internal biases that perpetuate caste discrimination. By weaving personal histories with broader social injustices, the book offers a stark reminder of Nepal’s lingering caste hierarchies and the human cost of economic exploitation. The review praises the author’s vivid storytelling while noting the unsettling relevance of the themes to contemporary Nepalese society.

articles.title: Fiction Park: They left a city and found a home
articles.summary: A Kathmandu family learns of an empty ancestral property from an old friend and decides to leave the capital to settle in the rural area known as Fiction Park. The story follows their journey of leaving urban life, confronting challenges of rebuilding on inherited land, and rediscovering community ties and a simpler way of living. It highlights themes of migration, heritage, and the search for a sustainable home away from the city’s pressures.

articles.title: Indian TV coverage of Nepal floods criticised for sensationalism
articles.summary: Indian television networks covering the recent floods in Nepal have faced criticism from local residents who say the crews turned their own hardships at disaster sites into sensational drama, focusing more on spectacle than on the victims. The article highlights concerns that the coverage prioritizes ratings over humanitarian reporting, and it raises questions about cross‑border media responsibility during crises.
